arithmetic.prediction: sighted saturates at budget 3; below 3 it cannot compare

blind_sighted.label: sighted with read budget 0 — no neighbours to compare

metrics.note: same trace as `stay`: a sighted organism that cannot read does what a blind one does

fires.evidence: sighted at budget 3 survives 114.6 of 120, at budget 1 survives 76.3

silent.evidence: stay and random produce the same trace hash at budget 0 and budget 1: stay 870435c692217f1f / 870435c692217f1f, random 98cc101a40bd8a2e / 98cc101a40bd8a2e

specific.evidence: saturation exactly at the counted number 3: budget 3 = 114.6, budget 4 = 114.6 (equal), budget 2 = 109.2 (lower); a blind sighted organism reproduces `stay` exactly (870435c692217f1f), so the arm that carries the effect is the one that reads, not the label

verdict.reason: counted reads per step (sighted = 3); saturation at exactly 3 on a uniform field (114.6 = 114.6); non-monotone on a gradient (budget 1 = 56.9, budget 2 = 0.0); non-reading policies unchanged by construction (same hash).

limitations: What this does not prove: that 3 is the right budget for any policy other than sighted (it is the counted minimum for comparing three cells); that partial sight is always worse than none (measured on one field shape, ten seeds); that reading has a cost (here it is free but limited — a model where reading costs energy is a different medium and has not been measured); that 0 survivors at budget 2 on a gradient is a law (the mechanism — walk one way, never correct — is the claim, the number 0 is an observation).
One read is worth a lot to `remember` (11 -> 84 survivors), but this compares two budgets only; it does not show the memory is the mechanism, only that without a read the memory never fills.
